sense: how much of something there is

terms.gloss: the amount, the measure of a thing
evidence: Hor. S. 2.6.1: modus agrī nōn ita magnus
Cic. Att. 13.33.2: dē modō agrī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The measure of a thing: its size or quantity (Lewis & Short). In speech Latin more often asks quantum with a genitive: quantum operae, how much effort; tantum vīnī, so much wine.

terms.grammar: noun, third declension: accusative vim, ablative vī
terms.gloss: a large amount, a mass (with a genitive)
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.91: magna vīs aurī argentīque

terms.comment: Post-Augustan, and mostly technical: Vitruvius, the elder Pliny, Quintilian (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: hoc erat in vōtīs: modus agrī nōn ita magnus
phrases.english: this is what I prayed for: an amount of land not so very big

phrases.latin: Sōcratēs, in pompā cum magna vīs aurī argentīque ferrētur, «Quam multa nōn dēsīderō!» inquit.
phrases.english: When a great amount of gold and silver was being carried in a procession, Socrates said: “How many things I don’t need!”

phrases.latin: sī, quantum operae sūmpsistī ut tuus pistor bonum faceret pānem, ejus duodecimam philosophiae dedissēs, ipse bonus jam prīdem essēs factus
phrases.english: if you had given philosophy a twelfth of the amount of trouble you took to get your baker to make good bread, you would long ago have become good yourself
